name: Cham Islands
provinceNote: Xã Tân Hiệp, Da Nang, the islands off Hoi An.
summary: A small group of forested islands off Hoi An, reached by a morning boat from Cua Dai. Explore the protected marine reserve, visit the Hai Tang pagoda, and eat fresh fish and sun-dried squid in Bai Lang village. Most people come for the day; a homestay night suits those who want the island once the day boats leave.
timeNeeded: A landing day, or a night in Bai Lang
fee: 70,000 VND per person per visit from 10 June 2026. The boat fare is separate. Boat fare: Check on arrival. Snorkel price: Check on arrival.
getThere: Boat from the Cửa Đại pier.
bestMonths: Summer, holidays, and Tết are the crowded pier months in the 2023 report
seoTitle: Cham Islands — the boat from Hoi An to a forested island
seoDescription: Take the boat from Hoi An’s Cửa Đại pier to forested Hòn Lao. Snorkel only in the water the 2026 letter opens. The visit fee is 70,000 VND from 10 June 2026 and does not include the boat.
intro: You take the morning boat from Hoi An’s Cửa Đại pier and land looking at Hòn Lao: the forested ridge, the houses on the shore, and the boats in the same view. Hòn Lao is the largest island and the only one with residents. A night here is a village house in Bai Lang after the day boats have gone back to Cửa Đại. Most of the 30 August 2023 pier report is a day crowd, not a hotel night.

Stay if the hamlet after that crowd leaves is the trip. Go back to Hoi An if you wanted the old town, and do not put My Son on the same morning as the 08:00 pier. The city temple page puts Hải Tạng about 20 km from the Hoi An shore. The biodiversity agency says the commune is 18 km from Hoi An.

The visit fee is 70,000 VND per person per visit from 10 June 2026, collected for the nature reserve. It does not include the boat. The 17 July 2020 reserve decision names seven islands: Hòn Lao, Hòn Cụ, Hòn Khô, Hòn Lá, Hòn Dài, Hòn Mồ, and Hòn Tai. The city page on 30 June 2026 says the cluster is eight islands. Snorkel only where the 23 January 2026 letter opens the water. The strict zone is closed to swimming and snorkeling. A tourism boat may not anchor on coral or seagrass.

Bai Lang is the landing. Hải Tạng stands in Xóm Cấm there, facing the fields called Đồng Chùa. It was built in 1758 and moved in 1848. Breakfast stalls line the Bai Lang coast road, and the 15 September 2025 study puts the evening meal around 17:00–18:00.
gettingAround: Fly into Da Nang International, which the civil-aviation AIP lists as VVDN, southwest of the city and 3.2 km from the city centre. There is no station on the island. The boat leaves from bến thủy nội địa Cửa Đại – Cù Lao Chàm. On 30 August 2023 the Border Guard described passengers from 08:00, a crowd from 08:00 to 10:00, and life jackets checked before a boat is cleared.
Land at Bai Lang. Hải Tạng, the founders’ hall, and the whale shrine are in that hamlet. The well and Âm Linh are in Bai Ong. The nest-trade temple is in Bai Huong. On the island, walk.

stayAreas.name: Bai Lang
stayAreas.summary: Sleep in a village house here if you want the shore after the day boats leave. Bai Huong and Bai Ong are the other hamlets on the same island. No hotel brand is a pick.

eat: The daily plate is the catch: fish, shrimp, squid, and swimming crab, with rice and little spice. Breakfast stalls line the Bai Lang coast road and the area by the well. Lunch sits around 11:00–12:00 and the evening meal around 17:00–18:00 on the 2025 study. Mực một nắng is the squid dried one sun. No stall price was printed.
interestsBody: Dining is the coast-road breakfast and the catch, not a Hoi An old-town menu. The food guide is that plate.
The island is Hòn Lao from the boat: ridge, shore, and the boats.
Snorkel in the water the 23 January 2026 letter opens. The strict zone is closed to swimming and snorkeling. A boat may not anchor on coral or seagrass.
Hải Tạng is the pagoda you can photograph. The well, the whale shrine, the founders’ hall, Âm Linh, and the nest temple are ranked halls in the hamlets.

body: Hòn Lao is the largest island and the only one with residents.
The boat leaves bến thủy nội địa Cửa Đại – Cù Lao Chàm. On 30 August 2023 passengers were described from 08:00, with the crowd from 08:00 to 10:00.

cards.title: Hòn Lao from the water
cards.summary: The forested ridge and the rocky shore, seen from the sea. The visit fee is not the boat fare.

blocks.heading: The ridge from the boat
paragraphs: The picture is the island through the center: forest, shore, and sea. The morning boats use the Cửa Đại pier. Life jackets are checked before a boat is cleared.
The 2020 reserve names seven islands. The 30 June 2026 city page says eight, and about 15 km² of land.

interestGroups.title: Water with a line on the map
interestGroups.summary: Snorkel only where the 2026 letter opens the water. The strict zone is closed.
body: The 23 January 2026 letter names snorkel swimming on the service-zone shores and in the restoration water, and it closes the strict zone to swimming and snorkeling. Scuba, stand-up paddle, kayak, and glass-bottom boats are named for that same restoration water. A business needs a permit from the culture and sports department.

The 17 July 2020 regulation does not list tourism in the strict zone. It allows ecotourism in the restoration zone only when it does not harm the fishery or the marine ecosystem, and it forbids tourism boats from anchoring on coral or seagrass. The 70,000 VND visit fee is separate from the boat.

cards.title: Shore and clear water
cards.summary: Clear water against the island. Snorkel only in the water the letter opens.

blocks.heading: Where a boat may stop
paragraphs: Restoration water named in the 2020 regulation includes Rạn Mành, part of Hòn Tai, Bãi Nần on Hòn Lao, Rạn Mè – Bãi Ông, and Hòn Dài. The 2026 letter also names snorkel swimming at Bãi Xếp, Bãi Chồng, Bãi Bìm, Bãi Hương, and the named water at Hòn Dài.

Strict water in the 2020 regulation includes Hòn Tai, Bãi Tra on Hòn Lao, the north of Hòn Lao, Hòn Mồ, Hòn Lá, and Hòn Cụ with Hòn Khô. The 2026 letter closes the strict zone to swimming and snorkeling.

interestGroups.title: Hải Tạng and the ranked halls
interestGroups.summary: Walk to the pagoda after you land in Bai Lang.
body: Hải Tạng faces Đồng Chùa. It was built in Cảnh Hưng 19 (1758), about 200 metres northeast of today’s site, and moved in Tự Đức 1 (1848). The city page adds a 2002 repair, a lotus pond, and a 3.5 metre Quan Âm in front of the three-door gate. National relic, 2006.
The same heritage list names the founders’ hall, the whale shrine, the Xóm Cấm well, the nest-trade temple, and Âm Linh.

cards.title: Hải Tạng Pagoda
cards.summary: The gate, the statue, and the hill in one frame.

blocks.heading: The pagoda above Đồng Chùa
paragraphs: Walk through Bai Lang after you land. The pagoda serves the islanders and, on the heritage pages, the trading ships that stopped to pray. Read 1758 and 1848 as two dates: built, then moved after storm damage.
The island visit fee is 70,000 VND per person per visit from 10 June 2026.

faqs.q: Does the 70,000 VND visit fee include the boat?
faqs.a: Resolution 16/2026/NQ-HĐND sets 70,000 VND per person per visit from 10 June 2026, collected for the Cu Lao Cham reserve. The boat is a separate fare.

season.label: Check the pier
season.note: The 30 August 2023 Border Guard report ties the crowd to summer, holidays, and Tết, with passengers from 08:00 and the crush from 08:00 to 10:00. It does not name a month when the pier closes. Cầu Ngư is a lunar rite at the whale shrine, not that crowd calendar. The visit fee is waived on four Tết days, 29 March, 26 May, and 2 September. The boat is still a separate charge.
